Founded by neuroscientists and technologists, we serve as a nexus for research collaboration, education, and public discourse on the path toward preserving and extending human cognition.
Our work spans multiple disciplines including neuroscience, computer science, nanotechnology, and philosophy. Through workshops, webinars, publications, and community building, we bring together researchers, students, and enthusiasts who share our vision of developing technologies that may one day allow for the precise mapping and functional recreation of neural architectures. We believe that whole brain emulation represents not only a profound scientific challenge but also a potential pathway to extending human experience, knowledge, and consciousness beyond current biological limitations.
For over 15 years, we have been at the forefront of research and development in this field, fostering collaboration between leading neuroscientists, technologists, and visionaries who share our mission. Our efforts have been powered by a dedicated community—over 100 volunteers have contributed to our initiatives over the years, with 30+ actively driving our programs forward today.

Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.
As a Perception Machine Learning Engineer, you will build the intelligent systems that "see" the world, directly shaping the future of autonomous travel.
Within the Perception team, we are tackling some of the most complex, open-ended challenges in autonomous driving. Our models must constantly adapt and improve as our fleet encounters the vast, unpredictable realities of public roads. We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to help design and build the automated, closed-loop systems that drive this continuous improvement.
In this role, you will be the bridge between model architecture and large-scale data infrastructure. You will leverage active learning and sophisticated data curation strategies to ensure our perception models are always learning from the most informative examples. Crucially, this means managing the entire lifecycle of our data: intelligently selecting novel scenarios from the fleet while continuously pruning our existing corpus to maximize training efficiency.
In this hybrid role you will report to a Technical Lead Manager.
You Will
Architect Infrastructure: Design and scale the data pipelines needed to mine, ingest, and manage massive volumes of sensor data from our fleet.
Drive Model Improvement: Deploy active learning algorithms to continuously identify and select the most impactful data for training, ensuring our large models continuously adapt to new environments with incremental updates.
Ensure Model Quality: Develop methods and recipes for evaluating real-world performance of our models, and detecting regressions in model updates. Develop and maintain ground-truth free performance metrics.
Optimize Data Efficiency: Conduct large-scale experiments focused on data balancing, subset selection, and label quality optimization. Lead automated curation strategies—including smart pruning and downsampling—to minimize dataset bloat and maximize compute efficiency.
Solve Long-Tail Challenges: Develop robust mining, training and evaluation pipelines for rare, safety-critical real-world scenarios.
Innovate with Model Signals: Utilize uncertainty estimation, confidence scores, and embedding space analysis to uncover model blind spots and guide automated data acquisition.
Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Work closely with researchers and operations teams to iterate on the end-to-end model development lifecycle.
You Have
A bachelor’s degree in Machine Learning, Robotics, or Computer Science. 3+ years of professional experience in Machine Learning and/or Computer Vision.
Proven, hands-on experience applying active learning in production environments.
Strong expertise in building large-scale ML data pipelines (mining, extraction, auto-labeling, ingestion).
Deep understanding of data curation—balancing, core set selection, and sampling—to optimize model performance.
Proficiency in Python and deep learning frameworks (PyTorch or JAX).
Strong software engineering skills for writing robust, production-ready code.
We Prefer
An advanced degree (MS or PhD) in Machine Learning, Robotics, or Computer Science.
A record of publications at top-tier conferences (e.g., CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, ICML, ICLR, NeurIPS, IROS, RSS, AAAI, IJCV, PAMI).
Experience with C++
Experience building data-centric infrastructure from the ground up to accelerate model iteration cycles.

Four main areas, though they overlap more than the list suggests. Expect to work across them rather than inside one:
Motion planning
– computing collision-free paths through an environment.
Control

Perception

Manipulation

The Senior Backend Engineer will be a key contributor to ACPWB's Security & Compliance practice, working on internal systems performance and security that directly supports our compensation advisory work. This Senior Backend Engineer role requires someone who can own internal systems performance and security within Security & Compliance without waiting to be told what needs to be done. The internal data pipeline and ETL infrastructure is critical infrastructure, and the people who depend on it — our analysts, our clients, our firm — need it to work. You will use Terraform and AWS on Azure and on-premise hybrid environment to build and maintain systems that meet that standard.
The Senior Backend Engineer is responsible for the technical infrastructure that makes ACPWB's analytical work possible. The Security & Compliance team of 6 builds and maintains the internal data pipeline and ETL infrastructure that powers our advisory practice, and this role is central to ensuring that infrastructure is reliable, secure, and scalable. Our analytical staff depends on this work. So do our clients, indirectly. You will know both are counting on you.
Key Responsibilities
◆ Implement and maintain backup, recovery, and disaster preparedness procedures for the internal data pipeline and ETL infrastructure
◆ Contribute to code reviews, technical documentation, and engineering standards for the Security & Compliance team
◆ Design and enforce access controls, authentication policies, and data security protocols
◆ Develop and maintain BI dashboards and analytical reports for internal stakeholders using Terraform and AWS
◆ Develop APIs and integrations connecting the internal data pipeline and ETL infrastructure with third-party data sources and internal tools
Qualifications
Required

◆ Ability to prioritize technical work based on business impact and operational risk
◆ Experience with version control (Git), code review practices, and CI/CD pipelines

Preferred

◆ Experience with containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes)
◆ Familiarity with compliance requirements such as SOC 2, GDPR, or CCPA as they apply to data systems
◆ Prior experience in a professional services or advisory firm technology environment
◆ Familiarity with API design and RESTful service development
WHY ACPWB
ACPWB was not designed to be the largest firm in our space. It was designed to be the most credible one. That decision shapes everything — how we staff, what work we take, how we train our team, and how we respond when a client asks us to reach a conclusion we cannot intellectually support.
ACPWB was founded in Milwaukee in 2006 with a simple mandate: help working Americans understand and advocate for the compensation they deserve. Eighteen years later, that mandate has grown into a full-service research and advisory practice serving clients from early-stage employers to Fortune 50 enterprises — and we are still based in Milwaukee, because Milwaukee is genuinely underrated.

We begin with a brief application review, followed by a 30-minute phone screen. Qualified candidates proceed to a 90-minute interview with the hiring manager and a peer. At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. Raytheon brings the strength of more than 100 years of experience and renowned engineering expertise to meet the needs of today’s mission and stay ahead of tomorrow’s threat. We deliver solutions that help our nation and allies defend freedoms and deter aggression, creating a safer, more secure world. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defense.
Join Systems Engineering and Test Capabilities (SE&TC), a cross-disciplinary engineering team solving complex systems challenges across some of Raytheon’s most advanced guided, autonomous and sensor-integrated technologies. If you’ve engineered complex vehicles, robotics platforms, automated machinery, aerospace systems or embedded technologies, many of the systems engineering skills you’ve developed can translate directly to this work.
Based in Tucson, Arizona, SE&TC supports technologies spanning the seabed to space, including ship-launched systems such as Standard Missile® and Tomahawk®, surface-launched systems including Javelin® and Coyote®, air-launched systems such as AMRAAM® and StormBreaker®, and emerging technologies including hypersonics and space solutions.
As a Systems Engineer, you’ll apply that experience across the full Systems Engineering V lifecycle, shaping architecture, requirements, integration and verification for complex systems that must perform reliably under demanding conditions. You’ll collaborate across software, hardware, modeling, controls, navigation, sensors and test to bring these systems from concept through field performance.
In this role, that experience could translate to work including:
Developing and managing system and subsystem requirements across hardware and software.
Defining system architectures and interfaces using MBSE tools such as Cameo.
Guiding system-level integration across hardware, software, controls and embedded technologies.
Leading verification and validation activities to ensure system requirements are fully assessed.
Conducting trade studies and translating findings into data-driven engineering recommendations.
Troubleshooting complex system issues and supporting failure investigations.
Providing technical leadership, mentoring engineers and strengthening collaboration across disciplines.
This role is 100% on-site at our Tucson, AZ campus with the possibility of occasional travel.
What You Will Do
Systems Architecture & Requirements
Develop, maintain and improve system and subsystem requirements for hardware and software elements of complex guided and autonomous systems.
Create system architectures, interface definitions and design documentation using MBSE tools such as Cameo in collaboration with multidisciplinary product teams and subject matter experts.
Lead updates to system and subsystem requirements specifications, ensuring traceability to verification objectives.
Integration & Verification
Guide system-level integration, hardware/software alignment and cross-team collaboration throughout development and production.
Plan and execute verification and validation strategies, ensuring requirements are accurately assessed during qualification testing.
Conduct trade studies, present findings to technical leadership and customers, and help drive design decisions.
Support troubleshooting, failure analysis and performance evaluation across multiple system elements.
Support test equipment software integration and verification.
Support system performance analysis.
Collaboration & Technical Leadership
Work closely with systems, software, hardware, configurable logic, sensor and test engineering teams to resolve system issues and align development priorities.
Engage in technical discussions with customers throughout the engineering lifecycle.
Partner with suppliers and Supply Chain teams as the Responsible Engineering Authority (REA) for applicable procured components and assemblies.
Lead Systems Verification Reviews with the Chief Engineer, Lead Systems Engineer and Integrated Product Team leadership.
Mentor engineers, facilitate cross-team knowledge transfer and support onboarding using core Systems Engineering practices.
Conduct and participate in peer reviews, formal documentation releases and Technical Data Package (TDP) updates.
Additional Technical Responsibilities
Support Statistical Process Control assessments and hardware verification activities across missile sections, launch platforms and higher-level assemblies.
Contribute technical expertise throughout development, integration, production, troubleshooting and system maintenance.
Serve as a system-level technical resource for the program, building knowledge across requirements, architecture, integration and verification.
Qualifications You Must Have
Typically requires a Bachelor’s in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM preferred) and a minimum of 2 years of prior engineering experience.
Engineering experience in one or more of the following areas: Autonomy, Controls, Robotics, Navigation, Embedded Systems
